transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to stop checking my work. I do bookkeeping, and I keep going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again, even when I know I already checked them. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves because I feel like if I don’t check just one more time, something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you're not actively checking your work?

Yes. Even when I’m not checking right then, the thought keeps popping up that I missed some hidden mistake—like in payroll or taxes—and then someone’s check won’t go through or the firm will get in trouble. I’ll try to tell myself the numbers matched, I saw it, but it comes right back, like I can’t trust my own eyes.
Is this need to check and recheck something that happens only with your work, or do you find yourself doing similar things in other parts of your life?

It’s mostly with work. The spreadsheets and calculations are where I get stuck. I’ll check them, and then I’ll go back and check again, and sometimes I’m still there hours after everyone else leaves. I know I already looked, but it feels like if I don’t do it one more time, something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
How much distress do these repeated checks cause you?

It’s really upsetting. I know I’ve already checked the spreadsheet or the calculations, but I still feel like I have to go back one more time. If I don’t, I get this strong feeling that something bad will happen and it’ll be my fault. It gets bad enough that I’ll stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves, just checking the same things over and over.
Are these checking behaviors affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Yes, it is. I’ve stopped making it to choir rehearsals and some youth-center commitments because I can’t get out of the office on time. And at work it’s gotten bad too—I missed a filing deadline and got called into a formal meeting about it. It’s embarrassing, and I feel like I’m letting people down.
What happens when you're unable to check your work one more time, do you feel a significant amount of anxiety?

Yes. If I can’t check it again, I get really anxious. Even if I know I already went over the spreadsheet or the calculations, it feels like I’m leaving something dangerous unfinished. I keep thinking that if something goes wrong, it’ll be my fault, so I end up going back over it again and again.
Do these thoughts about missing a mistake in your work feel like they are coming from outside of yourself, or are they more like your own worries?

They feel like my own worries, not like someone is putting them in my head or anything. It’s more like… even after I know the numbers match, this thought jumps in that I missed some hidden mistake in payroll or taxes, and then I start thinking someone’s check won’t go through or the firm will get in trouble. I try to push it away, but it comes right back, like I can’t trust what I just checked.
Are your repeating thoughts always about preventing some kind of mistake or harm from happening?

Mostly, yes. It’s usually about me missing one hidden mistake in the payroll or taxes, even when I already know the numbers match. I’ll try to push the thought away, but it comes right back, like I can’t trust my own eyes, and then I start thinking somebody’s check won’t go through or the firm will get in trouble.
Are your checks always aimed at preventing something specific from happening, like a financial error or legal trouble?

Yes, usually. It’s like I’m checking to stop something bad from happening. I keep going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations, even when I already checked them, because if I don’t do it one more time, I feel like I might miss something and it’ll be my fault. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves just checking again.
Do you ever feel like you need to perform these checks in a specific way or order to feel right, even if it doesn't necessarily relate to preventing a mistake?

Not really in a special order, no. It’s more that I feel like I have to go back over the spreadsheets and calculations again and again. Even if I already checked them, I’ll think, “If I don’t do it one more time, something bad could happen and it’ll be my fault.” Sometimes I end up staying at work for hours after everyone leaves just checking the same things.
Do you feel like you have to check your work again because you feel compelled to, even if you know it's already correct?

Yes. I know it’s already correct most of the time, but I still feel like I have to check it again. I’ll go back over the same spreadsheets and calculations over and over, and if I try to stop, I get this feeling that something bad might happen and it’ll be my fault. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone leaves because I can’t let it go.
Do you feel like your checks need to be done in a way that feels 'just right' to you?

Not really “just right,” I don’t think. It’s more like I can’t stop myself from checking the spreadsheets and calculations again. Even if I already checked them, I feel like if I don’t do it one more time, something bad could happen and it would be my fault. Sometimes I end up staying for hours after everyone else leaves because I keep going back over it.
Do you feel like your checks are complete only when you've done them a certain number of times?

Not really a certain number, no. It’s more like I’ll tell myself, “just one more time,” but then after I check it, I still don’t feel okay. So I go back over the same spreadsheet or calculation again because I feel like if I stop too soon and something is wrong, something bad could happen and it would be my fault. Sometimes that keeps me there for hours.
Do you feel like your work or the way you check things has to be symmetrical or perfect in some way?

No, I don’t think it’s about being symmetrical or perfect like that. I haven’t really noticed needing things to look a certain way. It’s more just... I feel like I have to check, but not because it has to be arranged perfectly.
Do you feel like checking your work is a way to regain control when you feel overwhelmed or uncertain?

I guess maybe, but it doesn’t feel like control exactly. It’s more that when I’m uncertain, I can’t stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations. Even if I already checked them, I feel like I have to do it one more time, because if I don’t and something bad happens, it’ll be my fault. Sometimes I end up staying at work for hours after everyone else leaves.
Do you feel like your checking is driven more by the fear of something going wrong or by the desire to make sure everything is perfect?

It’s more fear something will go wrong. Even when the numbers match, I keep getting this thought that maybe I missed some hidden mistake in payroll or taxes, and then someone’s check won’t go through or the firm will get in trouble. I try to push it away, but it comes right back, like I can’t trust what I just saw.
Is your need to check your work repeatedly driven by wanting everything to be perfect, or is it more about avoiding a mistake?

It’s more about avoiding a mistake. Even when I can see the numbers match, I get this thought that maybe there’s one hidden error in payroll or taxes that I missed. Like someone’s check won’t go through, or the firm will get in trouble, and it’ll be because I didn’t catch it. I try to ignore it, but it comes back and I feel like I can’t trust what I just looked at.
Is your main goal when checking your work to ensure everything is perfect or to avoid making any mistakes?

It’s more to avoid making mistakes. I’m not really trying to make it perfect… I just can’t stop thinking that if I don’t check the spreadsheet or calculation one more time, something bad could happen and it would be my fault. Even after I’ve already checked it, I’ll go back again and again, sometimes for hours after everyone else leaves.
Is it the possibility of making a mistake that drives you to check your work repeatedly, rather than trying to make it flawless?

Yes. It’s not about making it flawless, exactly. It’s that I keep thinking if I don’t go back over the same spreadsheet or calculation one more time, something bad could happen and it would be my fault. I’ll already have checked it, but I still end up checking again and again, sometimes staying hours after everyone else leaves.
Is your repeated checking of work mostly because you fear making a mistake or because you want everything to be perfect?

It’s mostly because I’m afraid of making a mistake. I’m not trying to make everything perfect. I just keep feeling like if I don’t check the same spreadsheet or calculation one more time, something bad could happen and it’ll be my fault. Even after I’ve already checked, I end up going back again and again, sometimes for hours after everyone leaves.
